Desktop Publishing · Week 10 · Title

Folded work and print preparation: bleed, trim and safe area

Printers cut paper, and the cut is never perfect. Bleed, trim and the safe area protect your design.

Next Generation Genius · Year 1 · Foundation

Desktop Publishing · Week 10 · Goals

By the end of today

  • Explain bleed, trim and safe area
  • Set up a document with 3 mm bleed
  • Plan the panel order of a tri-fold brochure
Desktop Publishing · Week 10 · Idea 1

Understand it

A print shop prints on bigger paper and cuts it down — and the blade can move a millimetre or two.

  • Trim: where the paper is meant to be cut (the finished size).
  • Bleed: extend background colours and photos 3 mm beyond the trim, so a slightly-off cut never leaves a white edge.
  • Safe area: keep text and logos at least 3–5 mm inside the trim, so nothing important is cut off.

In Canva: File → Show print bleed; in Scribus: set bleed in Document setup.

Desktop Publishing · Week 10 · Idea 2

Understand it

A tri-fold brochure is one sheet folded into six panels. The front cover is on the outside right; the inside panels read left to right. Always make a paper mock-up before printing.

Desktop Publishing · Week 10 · Key words

Key words

Bleed
colour extended 3 mm past the trim
Trim
the finished size where paper is cut
Safe area
the zone that keeps text away from the cut
Desktop Publishing · Week 10 · Practice

Now you do it

  1. Mark bleed, trim and safe area on a printed page
  2. Set up a tri-fold with bleed in Canva or Scribus
  3. Fold a paper mock-up to check the panel order

Need a hand? Fold the mock-up first; number every panel before designing.

Done early? Find out what crop marks are and add them to your PDF in Scribus.

Desktop Publishing · Week 10 · Assessment

How you will be assessed

  • Why do designers extend background colour 3 mm past the trim line?
  • Put a tri-fold brochure's panels in reading order for someone picking it up.
  • Show your folded paper mock-up with every panel numbered, and your tri-fold document set up with 3 mm bleed and a safe area.

Your work is marked against the rubric, and you may be asked to explain your choices. Show your own thinking.
